title: Glossary
html:
Who this page is for: every participant. Whenever a word is unfamiliar during the lab, come back here to see what it is, what it affects (what goes wrong if it is set wrong or skipped) and where it is used later (which chapter and section, and which account does it). Ctrl+F (⌘F on macOS) is the fastest way to find a term.

The console has a glossary too: ? in the top bar → Glossary, or type the term into ⌘K. It explains general platform words only; for Agent-DLC words (criteria, golden set, gate …) this page is the reference.

The "Agent-DLC method and Launchpad architecture" chapter says criteria set and judge calibration; the console says criteria table and Calibration. They are the same things. This page and the lab steps use the console's names.

Quick index by phase

Phase Terms you meet here first
Before you start Five quality dimensions, workspace, roles and permissions, criteria.sign / golden.admit / judge.calibrate, separation of duties, release policy (gated)
Define Criterion, tier (red line / gate / observe), decided by (evaluator / metric), evaluator (LLM judge), golden-set source file, case tier, expected answer
Build Harness, Runtime, five-stage pipeline, knowledge base, registry and skills, Memory
Evaluate Criteria table, signing, effective gates, golden set, splits (dev / regression / holdout), curate and seal, cost guard, live / candidate endpoints, candidate, release gate, four gates, PASS / BLOCKED / INVALID, pass^k, confidence interval, labelling task, κ, calibration
Release Waiver, sign and release, block, roll back, release request, public API, Gateway, Cedar policy (LOG_ONLY / ENFORCE), A/B experiment, canary
Observe Drift watch, baseline, scorecard, what the standard still owes, decision history, intent view
Feed back Issue box, reviewer link, admission, candidate item, regression replay, online evaluation, next criteria version, fix ladder

1. The standard: criteria and the criteria table

Term What it is What it affects Where it is used
Five quality dimensions Cognition (does it know the business), quality (is the answer reliable), responsibility (is it safe and compliant), cost, performance The criteria table needs a criterion for every dimension, or a note n/a:<dimension> reason; otherwise it cannot be published Concepts explains them; Define §1 maps requirements; the scorecard shows them as tiles
Criterion One row of the criteria table: a checkable statement (e.g. "never promise a refund the policy does not allow") with an ID, dimension, tier, how it is decided, and a threshold The gate judges each one; drift watch, the scorecard and the coverage matrix all count per criterion; each golden-set item names the criteria it tests in criteria_ids Define §1, §4 design; Evaluate §1 entry (developer); Feed back §7 adds Q2
Criteria table (criteria set) All criteria of one agent, versioned (v1, v2 …): draft → published → signed Belongs to one agent: it cannot be created while no agent is running; a deployment locks the version published at that moment, and with no published table the gate refuses to evaluate (release.no_criteria); published versions are read-only, changes go into Open a new version Evaluate §1 draft and publish (developer); Evaluate §2 sign (biz-owner); Feed back §7 opens v2
Tier: red line / gate / observe How severe a criterion is. Red line: one violation blocks; gate: the pass rate or metric must reach the threshold; observe: recorded only A red line is never waivable and cannot be decided by an LLM judge (only by a metric, a code assertion or trajectory matching); at least one red line is required; a missed gate can be waived; observed criteria never change the verdict Define §1; Evaluate §1 step 4 tries a judge-decided red line; Evaluate §12 four gates
Decided by: evaluator / metric Whether a criterion is scored by an evaluator (a pass rate) or compared on a metric (latency P95, tokens per session) Cost and performance must be metrics; the only metrics are latency P95 (ms), cost per success (USD) and tokens per session Define §1; Evaluate §1
Signing The business owner confirms a published version: "this is our standard" Unsigned, every gate report is INVALID; the signer cannot be the version's creator or last editor; each new version needs signing again Evaluate §2, Feed back §7.2 (biz-owner, needs criteria.sign)
Effective gates The tile at the top of the criteria table, e.g. 2 / 6: how many of the criteria declared as gates can block right now Judge-decided gates only observe until a calibration finds them aligned Define §4; Evaluate §1, §17
Thresholds taken together The card that multiplies the judge-gate thresholds into All gates holding Each threshold can look reasonable while together they pass only a fraction of sessions; think about it before signing Evaluate §1 step 5
Repeats (k) and pass^k Run each item k times; it passes only if all k pass With k ≥ 2 declared on a criterion the gate judges pass^k; each extra repeat multiplies time and cost Define §4 (S2 has k = 2); Evaluate §11 k when running the gate

2. The evidence: the golden set

Term What it is What it affects Where it is used
Golden set Items (a question plus a person's expected answer) serving one criteria table, in three splits The gate follows agent → published criteria table → golden set to find its data; with no golden set, or an empty regression or holdout, the gate refuses (release.no_golden / release.empty_golden); admission needs the table to have a golden set Define §3 review the source file (biz-owner); Evaluate §3 create (developer); Cleanup §2.5 delete
Splits: dev / regression / holdout dev: iterate on it; regression: replayed by the gate and by drift watch; holdout: evaluated by the gate too, never tuned against dev never enters a release verdict; the holdout is written once; here 24 / 15 / 9 items Evaluate §4 table; Evaluate §6 dev; Evaluate §11 regression + holdout
Curate and seal Curate the splits: one call that stratifies the source file by case tier into the three splits; the holdout is sealed afterwards The only way to write the holdout, and only once; fix expected answers in the source file before curating Evaluate §4 (biz-owner, needs golden.admit)
Case tier The kind of item: known_good, known_bad, ambiguous, adversarial Curation stratifies by tier so each split has the same mix; the coverage matrix counts criterion × tier Define §3; Evaluate §4
Expected answer and its source (expected_source) The correct answer a person wrote; the source records who: annotator / consensus / adjudicated, or agent_observed when copied from the agent The expected answer is the standard itself and must be confirmed by someone who knows the business; agent_observed cannot enter the golden set Define §3; Feed back §3 admission rules
Coverage matrix The golden-set table of how many items each criterion has per case tier A criterion marked as having too few items has a pass rate that says little Evaluate §4 step 6; Observe §9 scorecard
Admission The queue that turns what production exposed (thumbs-down, issue box, reviewer corrections) into new golden-set items Writes only to dev or regression, never the holdout; each candidate is decided once; mark repeats as duplicates instead of admitting them again Feed back §3 (biz-owner, needs golden.admit)

3. Judges and calibration

Term What it is What it affects Where it is used
Evaluator / LLM judge A rule that scores the agent's answer: built-in (e.g. Builtin.Correctness), custom LLM judge, or code evaluator (Lambda) A criterion needs the evaluator's full ID; evaluators belong to no agent; editing an evaluator invalidates its calibration Define §2 creates three custom judges; Evaluate §1 puts them in criteria
Calibration Measuring whether an LLM judge may stand in for a person: two people label the same items blind, the result is compared with the judge, and a third person decides Only after "aligned" does a judge criterion block as a gate, within the validity period; "not aligned" or never calibrated only observes Evaluate §14–§17
Labelling task / blind labelling Items taken from one evaluation run; two named annotators each mark pass / fail / undetermined Annotators do not see the judge's verdict while labelling; an annotator cannot decide their own task (calibration.own_labels) Evaluate §14 create (admin); Evaluate §15 label (developer, sme)
κ (Cohen's kappa) Agreement between two raters. Human–human κ: the two annotators; judge–human κ: the judge versus people Low human–human κ means the criterion itself is unclear; judge–human κ under the floor (0.6 here) cannot be found aligned; when every item carries the same label κ proves nothing Evaluate §16; Observe §8 "agent or judge?"
Calibration validity How many days a calibration verdict holds (30 here) After it expires the criterion is back to observe until calibrated again Roles §6; Evaluate §5

4. Release

Term What it is What it affects Where it is used
Release policy / release mode Workspace setting: direct (a deployment goes live) or gated (a new version waits for the gate), plus calibration validity, κ floor and the cost guard Only an administrator can change it; preset to gated for this workshop Roles §6; Evaluate §5
Cost guard Two amounts in the release policy: above "confirm" the starter must confirm the cost, above "refuse" the run is refused (5 / 20 USD here) Enforced by the server (run.cost_over_limit); only an administrator can exceed it Evaluate §5, §10
live / candidate endpoints A gated agent's two named endpoints: live serves production, candidate holds the new version awaiting release After the move, a deployment updates only candidate, invisible to users; console chat and the public API use live; a new agent uses DEFAULT until moved, so deployments take effect at once Build §1.5; Evaluate §7 move (release-ops, needs release.sign)
Candidate / release record The version each redeploy creates after the move, and the record opened for it, freezing candidate + criteria version + golden-set versions The record is what release, block, waiver and rollback act on; publish the criteria table before redeploying Evaluate §8; Release §1
Release gate Replays the regression and holdout splits on the candidate and judges it against the criteria table Only PASS can be signed (release.gate_not_passed) Evaluate §11–§12 run and read (developer); Release §1
Four gates Fixed order: red lines → denominator → per-dimension gates → observed; the gate where the verdict stops lights up Red-line violation → BLOCKED, never waivable; incomplete denominator → INVALID; missed gate → BLOCKED, waivable; observed never changes the verdict Concepts; Evaluate §12
PASS / BLOCKED / INVALID The gate's three verdicts INVALID is not a failure but missing evidence (unsigned criteria, holdout not run, more than 5% undetermined); it cannot be waived — fix the evidence and open a new record Evaluate §12; Release §2
95% interval / too few items to tell The interval (Wilson) around each criterion's pass rate in the gate report; "too few items to tell" when the threshold falls inside it With few items the interval is wide and cannot yet say whether the bar is met Evaluate §12
Waiver A temporary exception for one gate criterion, with a reason, a risk owner and an expiry (30 days at most) Applies to "this criterion on this agent": every gate report within its lifetime counts it as Waived; red lines cannot be waived; approver ≠ requester; repeated waivers mean the standard itself is wrong Release §1.2–§1.3, §2 (developer requests, release-ops approves)
Sign and release / Block release-ops releases a PASS (or waived) candidate so live points at it, or blocks it The signer cannot be the record's requester, administrators included (release.self_sign) Release §1.4
Roll back Points live back at the previous version Deletes nothing; a note is required Release §1.5 (release-ops)
Release request (promotion) A release across workspaces (e.g. dev → prod) that freezes a release bundle A different thing from the gate; this workshop has one workspace, so no exercise Release §3

5. Production and feedback

Term What it is What it affects Where it is used
Drift watch Replays the regression split on live on a schedule, scores it with the same criteria table, and alerts against a baseline Saving the schedule pins the criteria version published at that moment — after a new version, come back and Save again; every run costs money, so turn it off at the end Observe §8 schedule; Feed back §4, §7.4; Cleanup §2.2 turn off
Baseline Rolling median of earlier runs' pass rates With fewer than 8 points, score alerts do not judge Observe §8
Scorecard The page the business owner reads: needs attention, last gate verdict, five dimensions, what the standard still owes, coverage Reads the most recent run; "0 of N gates" means the dimension has only uncalibrated judges Evaluate §13; Observe §9 (biz-owner)
What the standard still owes The scorecard list of uncalibrated judges, live waivers and the like While it is not empty the scorecard's numbers are not fully trustworthy Evaluate §13; Observe §9
Decision history (audit) Who signed the standard, curated or admitted items, decided calibration, approved waivers, released or rolled back Administrators only; the Standards sub-tab shows only records whose object is the selected agent Observe §9; Feed back §8 (admin)
Issue box / reviewer link The issue box gathers production feedback and open issues; a reviewer link is a no-login page where a domain expert marks answers wrong and writes the correct one A reviewer's correction becomes an admission candidate; the link is shown only once Feed back §2 (biz-owner creates, sme reviews)
Online evaluation Keeps sampling and scoring real production sessions Looks at real traffic, not the golden set; failing sessions do not enter admission automatically Feed back §6 (optional)
Intent view What users ask, grouped by an AI from each session's first message Group names can change between calls; Unanswered questions can be sent straight to the issue box — one of the ways into feedback Observe §6
Fix ladder The agent's recent criteria runs in order, comparing before and after a fix When the criteria versions differ it gives two numbers: the agent got better by (old standard) and the standard got harder by (new versus old), so a drop caused by a stricter standard is not counted against the agent Feed back §4, §7.4

6. Platform and build

Term What it is What it affects Where it is used
Workspace An isolated environment (one AWS account + Region) with its own agents, secrets, data and release policy This workshop has one workspace, default Setup §5
Managed Harness An agent loop hosted by AgentCore: pick a model, prompt and tools, no code No configuration-bundle A/B experiments Build §0, §2 (lab-policy-advisor)
Runtime / Strands (ZIP path) The AgentCore service that runs agent code; with Strands the platform generates Strands Agents code and deploys it as a zip The main agent uses it because the configuration-bundle contract that A/B experiments and canaries need is built only into platform-generated code Build §0, §1 (lab-service-assistant)
Five-stage pipeline generate → package → provision → deploy → register; every creation method ends here Deployment progress shows stage by stage on the agent page Build §1.4
Knowledge base A platform-managed searchable document store the agent answers from Test retrieval quality before attaching it; with or without it changes C1 and Q1 scores Build §4, §6, §7
Registry / skill The discovery layer cataloguing A2A agents, MCP tools and skills, draft → pending approval → published; a skill is a reusable instruction pack Only published records can be attached to an agent; here the business owner approves by convention, because a skill decides how the agent talks to customers Build §5 (developer submits, biz-owner approves)
Memory Lets the agent remember the current conversation and, optionally, each user's long-term information (such as preferences) Partitioned by agent + user: a preference told to one agent does not show up in another agent's answers; inspect it on Memory (/v3/memory) Build §8
Gateway / Cedar policy A Gateway turns APIs and tools into MCP tools the agent can call; Cedar policies decide who may call which tool actions. LOG_ONLY records, ENFORCE blocks ENFORCE is default-deny: with no ACTIVE permit policy every agent using that Gateway loses all its tools, so gather evidence under LOG_ONLY first Release §5 (admin); Observe §7 policy decision logs
Public API / API key Business systems call agents through /v1/... with an X-Api-Key header, on the same call path as console chat A gated agent is called only on live; this is the demo / PoC path, see the appendix for production Release §4; Production integration
A/B experiment / configuration bundle Swaps prompts on the same Runtime through a configuration bundle and replays a dataset to compare two groups Does not split real users; a promotion's deployment in a gated workspace still goes through the gate Release §6 (optional)
Runtime canary Shifts real production traffic to the candidate in steps Bypasses the gate — do not use it on a gated agent Release §7 (optional)

7. Roles and permissions

Term What it is What it affects Where it is used
Roles: admin / operator / member The console's only three roles: platform administrator, release operations, member; each has default permissions An administrator can grant or revoke single permissions per account Roles §1
Five preset accounts admin, developer, biz-owner, release-ops, sme, configured from the roles above plus extra grants Every "who does it" in the chapters names one of these; each chapter's prerequisites list the browser sessions to prepare Roles §1; Teams
criteria.sign / golden.admit / judge.calibrate Signing criteria tables, curating and admitting golden-set items, deciding calibration Not carried by any non-admin role; granted to named people only (biz-owner here); accounts without them do not see the buttons Roles §1; Evaluate §2, §4, §16
release.sign / waiver.approve Release, block, roll back and move endpoints; approve waivers Defaults of the operator role; a developer call gets 403 Evaluate §7; Release §1–§2
Separation of duties Enforced by the server by username: one person cannot both request and sign Criteria signer ≠ the version's creator or last editor; release signer ≠ requester (administrators included); waiver approver ≠ requester; calibration decider ≠ annotator (administrators included) Roles §7; Release §2
